title: "Literature review"
bibliography: ../references.bib

**Plan:** `plans/plan-001.yaml` (section `literature`). **Review date:** 2026-11-12.
**Scope:** the 12 seed papers listed in the plan, plus 13 primary papers added on
CT-number-to-density conversion, deep-learning density and material estimation,
how XCAT/DukeSim phantoms encode texture, and conditional diffusion compared with
deterministic regression.

**Reading rule.** Every statement below comes from text that was actually read. For
each paper the access level is given as *full text* or *abstract only*, and nothing is
claimed beyond what that level supports. The "Not accessed" section lists the gaps.

## 1. Dataset and simulator facts (TrueCT and DukeSim)

This section collects the concrete facts needed to build training targets. The
sources are @truect_challenge (full text, PMC11973969) and @dukesim (full text,
PMC6598436). Facts from the companion phantom papers are labelled with their own
sources.

### 1.1 Phantom construction (emphysema cohort)

- **Cohort.** The challenge used 200 models: 67 emphysema, 67 lung-lesion and 66
  liver-lesion. The 67 emphysema models came from 67 randomly chosen COPDGene Phase I
  patient CTs (32 female; age 62 ± 9 years; BMI 28.7 ± 6.0 kg/m²)
  [@truect_challenge]. **These are not drawn from the original XCAT library.** Only
  the liver-lesion models were built from existing XCAT phantoms. The emphysema
  models were built from new segmentations in the XCAT style.
- **Segmentation.** Major organs (body, bones, lungs, heart, liver) were segmented with
  commercial software. Airways, pulmonary vessels and emphysematous regions were
  segmented with a University of Iowa algorithm. The masks were meshed with VTK
  marching cubes, then smoothed and remeshed in Rhinoceros ("Smooth", then
  "QuadRemesh") [@truect_challenge]. Phantom boundaries are therefore smoothed meshes,
  not the original segmentation voxels.
- **Voxel size.** All 200 models were voxelized at **0.25 mm isotropic**
  [@truect_challenge]. @abadi_2019_bones gives the reason for this choice: 0.25 mm is
  about half the detector-element size of a clinical scanner.
- **Texture.** "Trabecular bone texture and lung parenchyma were incorporated using
  anatomically informed statistical models" [@truect_challenge]. The challenge cites
  @abadi_2019_bones, @abadi_2018_lung and @abadi_2017_lung_spie for these models:
  - *Trabecular bone* [@abadi_2019_bones, full text]. Cortical bone is a morphological
    erosion of the bone mask, with thickness measured per phantom from its source CT.
    Trabecular texture comes from 3-D power-law noise synthesis, with spectral
    exponents fitted to Visible Human Female data and binned **uniformly into five
    levels**. In that paper's simulation the five levels were assigned trabecular-bone
    densities of **1.00, 1.07, 1.14, 1.21 and 1.28 g/cm³**. Trabecular density
    is therefore a small set of discrete density bins carried by separate voxel
    materials, not a continuous field.
  - *Lung* [@abadi_2018_lung, abstract; @abadi_2017_lung_spie, abstract]. Airways,
    arteries and veins were grown to terminal branches by a volume-filling algorithm.
    The 2018 paper reports about 46,000 airways, 45,000 arteries and 40,000 veins per
    phantom. The parenchyma is modelled as polyhedral secondary pulmonary lobules with
    interlobular-septa borders. Inside each lobule is a heterogeneous background from
    non-parametric texture synthesis, informed by a high-resolution lung-specimen CT.
    The number of parenchymal material bins was **not stated in the abstracts read**.
    It must be found from the phantom label tables in E00.
- **Material definition.** Each organ or structure was assigned a density and an
  elemental composition from **ICRU Report 46**. Between patients, the "average
  density values (per ICRU report)" were varied "in the range of ± 15 HU"
  [@truect_challenge]. The emphysema regions were defined at **−950 ± 17 HU (range
  −918 to −979 HU)** [@truect_challenge]. The 67 lung-lesion models were built from a
  separate set of 67 COPDGene cases [@truect_challenge]. Pairing must confirm that the
  local 67 are the emphysema subset.
- **How emphysema density was set (precursor study).** In the 20-phantom emphysema
  study by @abadi_2023_emphysema (full text), emphysema voxels used the elemental
  composition of lung parenchyma. Their density was derived from the mean HU measured
  in the eroded emphysema mask of the source COPDGene CT, using
  ρ = μ / (μ/ρ)~lung parenchyma~. **"Each XCAT phantom had one density assigned to the whole emphysema
  regions. The same approach was also used to assign lung density for the lung
  parenchyma for each case."** The ground-truth lung and emphysema values in that
  study were −880.0 ± 37.9 HU and −969.2 ± 22.7 HU. *Inference:* the TrueCT challenge
  reports emphysema HU per case. If it used the same method, emphysema density is one
  scalar per subject, taken from that subject's material table. This must be
  confirmed against the local tables.
- **How materials reach the simulator.** DukeSim takes two inputs: a voxelized
  phantom and a parameter file describing the scanner and protocol. Linear
  attenuation coefficients μ~m,E~ are computed per *material* and energy bin with
  xraylib, and ray-traced as path length times μ per material [@dukesim]. The
  simulator interface is therefore **material label plus material definition
  (composition and density)**, not a free-form density map. This is consistent with
  the plan's DukeSIM contract. The exact local file format still has to be verified.

### 1.2 Acquisition (Duke-1 generic scanner)

From @truect_challenge, Table 1 and §2.2:

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Detector | Energy-integrating, Gd₂O₂S scintillator, 0.8 mm thick, 7.8 g/cm³, gain 50 photons/keV |
| Detector columns × rows | 900 × 64 |
| Projections per rotation | 1000 |
| Detector element / focal spot | 1 × 1 mm / 1 × 1 mm |
| Source–isocenter / source–detector | 575 mm / 1075 mm |
| Trajectory | Helical, pitch 1.0 |
| Spectrum | **120 kV**, measured bowtie profile |
| Tube current | Tube current modulation (validated technique) |
| **Dose levels** | **50–150 mAs in 25 mAs steps** (5 levels; the per-case assignment is not tabulated in the paper) |
| Physics | Ray-traced primary, Monte Carlo scatter, focal-spot wobble, anti-scatter grid, beam-hardening correction |
| Output | DICOM-CT-PD sinograms, with per-projection tube current and water attenuation coefficient in the headers |

DukeSim's beam-hardening correction is a fourth-order polynomial water correction
fitted from mono-energetic water simulations [@dukesim].

### 1.3 Reconstructions

- **The challenge shared sinograms, not images.** Participants reconstructed the
  images themselves. The organisers reconstructed all 200 sinograms with the MCR
  toolkit, but only for quality control (artifact inspection). They also checked CT
  numbers on water-phantom and ACR-phantom simulations [@truect_challenge].
- **Requested reconstruction format** [@truect_challenge, Table 2]:
  - field of view **500 mm**;
  - in-plane pixel size **500/512 ≈ 0.977 mm**;
  - slice thickness **0.55 mm** for chest cases (1.5 mm for liver cases);
  - slice interval equal to slice thickness, with no overlap;
  - full z-coverage;
  - DICOM format.
- **No kernel is specified.** The five submitted methods differed widely: MBIR,
  Katsevich, FBP followed by algebraic (BiCGSTAB) updates, FDK, and fan-beam FBP with
  per-task ramp cut-offs at 90/60/40 % of Nyquist [@truect_challenge]. The paper does
  not say which reconstruction, if any, is redistributed with the dataset.
  **The provenance, kernel and HU calibration of the local `recons/` must be
  established in E00. Nothing in the literature fixes them.**
- **HU calibration.** The paper reports only that CT numbers were "verified in the
  water phantom and in the inserts of the ACR phantom" [@truect_challenge]. It gives
  no numerical calibration result.

### 1.4 Ground truth and scoring in the challenge

- The digital ground truth was **"the mono-energetic representation of the human
  models in HU at the effective energy (i.e., 64 keV)"** of the acquisitions
  [@truect_challenge]. @abadi_2023_emphysema used 67 keV for a Siemens Flash model,
  computed during the beam-hardening-correction step.
- For scoring, reconstructions were **upsampled to the 0.25 mm phantom grid by linear
  interpolation**. RMSE and SSIM were computed in the lung-parenchyma VOI for
  emphysema cases. SSIM dynamic range was set to the ground-truth HU range
  [@truect_challenge].
- Emphysema results across the 5 participants: SSIM 0.22–0.78 and **RMSE 77.6–186.7
  HU** (absolute range). Error depended on emphysema severity, because more severe
  cases had lower RMSE [@truect_challenge].
- The ground truth was withheld from participants. It "can be obtained by contacting
  the corresponding author" [@truect_challenge].

### 1.5 Implications for target construction (inferences, to verify in E00)

1. Density is largely piecewise-constant per material label. The exceptions are
   textured materials (trabecular bins, lung-parenchyma texture), which are encoded as
   *additional labels*, not as continuous values. A label-to-table density map
   (A07, `label_to_table_density`) is therefore physically natural. Density-only and
   label-only targets may carry nearly the same information, apart from the
   per-subject table values.
2. The per-subject variation of ±15 HU around ICRU 46 values corresponds to small
   density changes for soft tissue. Its exact size depends on the material and has
   not been computed here. The per-subject emphysema density is a single scalar in a
   narrow range (−918 to −979 HU). Recovering subject-specific table entries from CT
   is a per-region mean-estimation problem, which voxelwise losses may not capture.
3. The CT grid is about 0.98 × 0.98 × 0.55 mm and the phantom grid is 0.25 mm
   isotropic. At native phantom resolution, many of the roughly 130,000 vessel and
   airway branches per phantom [@abadi_2018_lung] are sub-voxel in CT. This supports
   keeping volume-fraction targets on the CT grid separate from native-grid labels
   (A14, A15).
4. Reconstructed lung HU is biased relative to ground truth. @abadi_2023_emphysema
   found the mean lung HU overestimated under every imaging condition, "mainly because
   of the presence of scatter". Lung MAE was 57–175 HU, and errors were larger at
   edges and in denser regions. A purely physical HU-to-density baseline will
   therefore carry a systematic lung bias unless it is calibrated on TRAIN.

## 2. Per-paper notes: seed papers

### @valand_2026 (abstract and publisher page only)
- **Task:** map spectral photon-counting CT images to a density map ρ and an
  effective atomic number map Z~eff~.
- **Input:** simulated abdominal PCCT at 4 energy thresholds, 2 dose levels,
  several iodine concentrations and 3 clinical kernels.
- **Ground truth:** the phantom truth of 32 training human models.
- **Model and loss:** a GAN, trained with and without a "physics-informed
  regularization loss". The loss is not defined in the abstract.
- **N:** 32 training models; 16 test phantoms; 6 clinical cases; a reader study on 30
  slices.
- **Headline results (with physics regularisation):** NRMSE 1.29 % for ρ and 0.68 %
  for Z~eff~; SSIM 0.99 and 0.99; PSNR 29.8 and 29.04 dB. Maximum RMSE on clinical
  data was 5.45 %. In the reader study, median conspicuity was 4.52 for the material
  maps against 4.13 for virtual monochromatic images.
- **Clinical claim:** the 6-case clinical check and the reader study. The authors
  note that the small sample limits generalisation.
- **Differences from our setting:** spectral rather than single-energy input; abdomen
  rather than chest COPD; outputs are ρ and Z~eff~, not DukeSim labels. The physics
  loss relies on multi-energy measurements, so it should not be transferred.
- **Not read:** architecture details, loss definitions, and any ablation of L1,
  Huber or gradient losses.

### @truect_challenge (full text)
See §1. **Task:** benchmark CT reconstruction against phantom truth. There was no
learning component, and no machine-learning submission was received. **Clinical
claim:** none beyond being "modeled based on clinical CT images". **Difference from
our setting:** the challenge scored reconstruction against 64 keV HU truth; we invert
reconstruction to materials and density.

### @dukesim (full text)
- **Task:** a CT simulator for voxel phantoms.
- **Physics:** ray-traced primary signal using per-material μ from xraylib. Scatter
  comes from a modified MC-GPU and is smoothed with a scatter kernel. The model also
  includes Gaussian quantum and electronic noise, detector crosstalk, 4 × 5
  focal-spot/detector subsampling, flying focal spot, bowtie filter and polynomial
  water correction.
- **Validation:** against a Mercury phantom on a Siemens Definition Flash at 120 kV,
  50/150/300 mAs, reconstructed with FreeCT (medium kernel, 0.6 mm slices, 512²
  pixels, 370 mm FOV). Relative errors: contrast 1.4 %; noise magnitude below 0.5 %;
  NPS average and peak frequency 2.49 % and 2.57 %; MTF f~50~ 3.1 % (air insert) and
  0.4 % (bone insert).
- **Runtime:** about 9 minutes per 3-rotation scan of a 1900 × 1900 × 1000-voxel,
  0.25 mm phantom on 4 Titan Xp GPUs.
- **Difference from our setting:** this is a forward model. It was validated on a
  cylindrical phantom only, and the authors list that as a limitation.

### @salinas_2025 (abstract only)
- **Task:** the *opposite* direction to ours. Two 3-D Double-U-Net conditional GANs
  generate 16 organ textures from homogeneous segmentations, producing heterogeneous
  phantoms that are then simulated in DukeSim.
- **N:** 378 CT–segmentation pairs from a public dataset, with 18 held out.
- **Results:** MAD 46.15 ± 1.06 HU, SSIM 0.86, PSNR 28.62, MMD 0.0016. These are
  improvements of 27 %, 5.9 %, 6.2 % and 28 % over homogeneous texturing.
- **Clinical claim:** none beyond visual resemblance.
- **Relevance:** shows that DukeSim accepts learned heterogeneous phantoms. Not read:
  how generated HU textures were turned into DukeSim materials. That conversion is
  exactly the interface question for our export step.

### @dukesim_copd_validation (full text via PMC excerpt)
- **Task:** validate DukeSim against a *physical* Kyoto Kagaku chest phantom fitted
  with pig-lung samples and NIST foams.
- **Data:** scanned on Siemens Force and Flash at 120 kV, CTDIvol 1.15–7.42 mGy,
  0.75 mm slices, wFBP or iterative reconstruction. The virtual phantom was built at
  0.25 mm. 28 simulations were reconstructed with vendor ReconCT.
- **Results:** mean biomarker difference 3.84 % (range 0.19–18.27 %) for LAA-950,
  LAA-856, Perc15, lung mass, volume and HU distributions. Pig-lung inserts were
  excluded "due to their unknown textures".
- **Clinical claim:** none, as it uses no patients.
- **Relevance:** sets the expected sim-to-real gap on lung biomarkers. It does not
  validate the TrueCT Duke-1 model specifically.

### @ron_mic_2015 (abstract)
- **Model:** encoder–decoder with skip connections, trained end-to-end "from very few
  images" with heavy augmentation.
- **Results:** won the ISBI 2015 cell-tracking challenge categories; segments a
  512 × 512 image in under 1 s.
- **Relevance:** the base architecture. It addresses segmentation, not quantitative
  regression.

### @cicek_2016 (abstract)
- **Model:** the 2-D U-Net with every operation replaced by its 3-D counterpart,
  trained from sparse annotation, with on-the-fly elastic deformation.
- **Data:** Xenopus kidney.
- **Relevance:** justifies the 3-D context arm of A04. No CT or regression results.

### @oktay_2018 (abstract)
- **Model:** attention gates added to a U-Net.
- **Results:** on two abdominal CT multi-class datasets, attention gates
  "consistently improve" U-Net across datasets and training sizes, at small cost.
- **Relevance:** the attention arm of A13.

### @nnunet_2021 (abstract; method details from preprint arXiv:1904.08128, full text)
- **What it is:** a self-configuring U-Net pipeline evaluated on 23 public
  segmentation datasets.
- **Training defaults:**
  - loss is "the sum of cross-entropy and Dice loss", which empirically improved
    training stability and accuracy;
  - 1000 epochs × 250 iterations;
  - SGD with Nesterov momentum 0.99, learning rate 0.01, poly decay;
  - deep supervision.
- **CT normalisation:** **global** (not per-image), clipping to the 0.5–99.5
  foreground percentiles and then applying the global foreground mean and SD,
  "as intensity values are quantitative".
- **Configurations:** 2-D, 3-D full-resolution and 3-D cascade, chosen by 5-fold
  cross-validation. The 3-D full-resolution configuration was best overall, but the
  best choice per dataset "can not be predicted with perfect accuracy".
- **Augmentation:** includes Gaussian noise, Gaussian blur and low-resolution
  simulation.
- **Relevance:** directly supports A04, A06 and A17 and the train-only global
  normalisation.

### @ho_2020 (abstract)
DDPM, trained on a weighted variational bound linked to denoising score matching.
Reports FID 3.17 on CIFAR-10. Defines our diffusion objective. Unconditional
natural-image generation only.

### @palette_2022 (abstract)
- **Model:** conditional image-to-image diffusion.
- **Results:** outperforms "strong GAN and regression baselines" on colourisation,
  inpainting, uncropping and JPEG restoration. Reports that **L1 versus L2 in the
  denoising objective affects sample diversity**, and that self-attention matters.
- **Relevance:** motivates A08 and A10. Natural images and perceptual metrics only;
  no quantitative-regression target.

### @ddim_2021 (abstract)
Non-Markovian sampler using the same training as DDPM. Produces samples 10–50×
faster and trades compute for quality. Directly supports A09.

## 3. Per-paper notes: expansion papers

### CT number to density and material conversion
- **@schneider_1996** (abstract). Introduces the stoichiometric calibration: fit the
  scanner's attenuation parameters on tissue-equivalent inserts, then compute the
  HU-to-electron-density (or stopping power) curve for real tissue compositions. It
  proved more precise than direct tissue-substitute calibration when checked by
  proton radiography of a biological sample.
- **@schneider_2000** (abstract). Splits the HU scale into sections. Within each
  section, mass density and elemental weights are interpolated with two-component
  mixture relations. Expected accuracy: **density better than 0.04 g/cm³**; P and Ca
  within 1 and 2.3 percentage points; H within 0.8 pp and N within 3 pp; but **C and O
  up to 14 pp**. This is the classical quantitative statement that single-energy CT
  fixes density far better than composition, which supports the plan's identifiability
  principle.

### Deep learning for density and material maps from single-energy CT
- **@gao_2023** (full text). SECT → mass density and RSP using a voxelwise ANN, an
  FCNN and a ResNet.
  - *Training:* only the CIRS 062M electron-density phantom (9 inserts,
    0.203–1.830 g/cm³).
  - *Testing:* Gammex 467, plus the CIRS M701 and M702 anthropomorphic phantoms
    (head–neck, thorax and pelvis protocols, 120 kVp).
  - *Whole-phantom results, M701 (Table 12):* FCNN mass-density MAPE in lung was
    1.57 %, against 8.29 % for stoichiometric calibration and 12.96 % for the
    voxelwise ANN. FCNN bone MAPE was 0.92 % against 3.17 %.
  - *Internal inconsistency:* the abstract attributes 12.96 % to the stoichiometric
    method in lung, but Table 12 gives 12.96 % to the ANN.
  - *Patients:* two patient scans were shown qualitatively, and one patient's mean
    densities are tabulated. There was no patient ground truth.
  - *Takeaway:* convolutional context beat the voxelwise mapping, especially in lung,
    which is direct evidence for A02.
- **@charyyev_2022** (abstract). SECT → synthetic high- and low-kV DECT with a
  residual attention GAN, on 70 head–neck patients with leave-one-out validation.
  MAE was 36.9 and 35.8 HU. SPR from a dual-energy stoichiometric method was within
  about 1 % NMSD of SPR from real DECT. Clinical data, but the target is a surrogate
  image rather than a material ground truth.

### XCAT and DukeSim phantom texture and material encoding
- **@abadi_2019_bones** (full text) and **@abadi_2018_lung** /
  **@abadi_2017_lung_spie** (abstracts): see §1.1.
- **@abadi_2023_emphysema** (full text), the closest precursor to the TrueCT COPD
  phantoms:
  - 20 phantoms (10 XCAT bodies × 2 emphysema renditions) at 0.25 mm;
  - ICRU 46 materials; one density per phantom for emphysema and for parenchyma;
  - simulated with DukeSim modelling a Siemens Flash at 20–100 mAs;
  - wFBP B31f/B46f/B70f and SAFIRE I31/I46/I70, 0.75 mm slices at 0.5 mm interval,
    0.48 mm pixels, 500 mm FOV;
  - ground truth was μ at the 67 keV effective energy, expressed in HU.
  - *Best condition* (100 mAs, I31): mean lung HU error 35 ± 3 HU, LAA-950 −4 ± 5 %,
    Perc15 26 ± 10 HU.
  - *Lung MAE* was 57–175 HU across conditions, larger at edges and in dense regions.

### Conditional diffusion compared with deterministic and adversarial regression
- **@lyu_2022** (abstract). DDPM and score-matching models with four samplers, used
  for MRI → CT. They "generate better synthetic CT images than the CNN and GAN
  models", and **averaging Monte Carlo samples improved results**. Dataset size and
  metrics were not read.
- **@wolleb_2021** (abstract). Diffusion segmentation conditioned on the image at
  every sampling step. Repeated sampling gives uncertainty maps and an implicit
  ensemble that "increases the segmentation performance" (BRATS 2020). Published at
  MIDL 2022 according to secondary sources. Cited here as the arXiv version, which is
  what was verified.
- **@blau_2018** (abstract). Proves that lowering mean distortion necessarily makes
  outputs more distinguishable from real images, for any distortion measure. This is
  the theoretical reason to expect a sample mean (A10) or a deterministic U-Net (A08)
  to win on MAE while losing realistic texture.
- **@moschetto_2025** (arXiv abstract snippet). With a shared U-Net backbone for T1w →
  T2w MRI, a GAN (Pix2Pix) outperformed the diffusion and flow-matching models. It is
  a counterexample to assuming diffusion wins on paired translation.

| @truect_challenge | Reconstruction benchmark | Sinograms (120 kV) | 64 keV HU phantom | n/a | n/a | RMSE 77.6–186.7 HU (emphysema) | None | Full |

| @gao_2023 | SECT → mass density, RSP | Real SECT of phantoms | Insert nominal values | ANN/FCNN/ResNet, voxel loss | 1 calibration phantom | Lung MAPE 1.57 % vs 8.29 % stoich. | Qualitative, 2 patients | Full |
| @charyyev_2022 | SECT → synthetic DECT | Clinical SECT, head–neck | Real DECT | Residual attention GAN | 70 patients (LOOCV) | MAE ≈ 36 HU; SPR ≈ 1 % | Retrospective patients | Abstract |
| @schneider_2000 | HU → ρ, elemental weights | SECT HU | Tissue tables | Piecewise interpolation | n/a | ρ < 0.04 g/cm³; C, O ≤ 14 pp | n/a | Abstract |
| @abadi_2023_emphysema | Protocol effects on quantification | DukeSim CT | 67 keV HU phantom | n/a | 20 phantoms | Lung HU bias 35 HU (best) | None | Full |
| @nnunet_2021 | Segmentation framework | Multi-modality | Manual labels | U-Net, CE + Dice | 23 datasets | SOTA on most | n/a | Abstract + preprint |
| @palette_2022 | Image → image | Natural images | Paired targets | Conditional diffusion | not read | Beats GAN and regression | n/a | Abstract |
| @lyu_2022 | MRI → CT | MRI | CT | DDPM / score models vs CNN, GAN | not read | Diffusion > CNN, GAN; averaging helps | n/a | Abstract |
| @moschetto_2025 | T1w → T2w | MRI | MRI | GAN vs diffusion vs flow matching | 3 public sets | GAN best | n/a | Abstract snippet |

None of these works addresses our exact setting: **single-energy, synthetic,
chest-COPD CT → DukeSim material labels plus density, with paired phantom truth.**
The closest are @gao_2023 (SECT → density, but trained on a calibration phantom) and
@valand_2026 (phantom-truth supervision, but spectral input).

## 5. Ablation rationale (A01–A19)

"Support" means a primary source read here bears directly on the contrast. Where the
plan's listed reference does not support the ablation, this is stated.

| ID | Supporting literature | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| A01 target representation | @dukesim (the simulator consumes material + composition, not density); @schneider_2000 (density is identifiable, composition weakly) | **Partial.** Motivates having labels at all. No paper compares density-only, label-only and joint training. @valand_2026 regresses two continuous maps, not labels; @salinas_2025 runs in the reverse direction. |
| A02 point baselines | @schneider_1996, @schneider_2000 (physical HU curve); @gao_2023 (voxel ANN vs FCNN vs stoichiometric: FCNN best, voxel ANN worst in lung) | **Good.** @valand_2026 does not bear on SECT baselines. |
| A03 filtered calibration vs U-Net | @gao_2023 (DL maps less noisy than stoichiometric); @abadi_2023_emphysema (scatter-driven lung bias that a TRAIN-fitted calibration must absorb) | **Partial.** @nnunet_2021, the listed reference, is not a rationale for this contrast. |
| A04 2D / 2.5D / 3D | @cicek_2016; @nnunet_2021 (3-D full-res best overall, but not predictably per task) | **Good**, for segmentation. No density-regression evidence. |
| A05 regression loss | @palette_2022 (L1 vs L2 changes diffusion sample diversity only) | **None for the deterministic contrast.** The listed @valand_2026 abstract mentions only a physics regulariser; L1, Huber and gradient terms are unsupported by anything read. |
| A06 CE vs CE + Dice | @nnunet_2021 (CE + Dice improved stability and accuracy empirically) | **Good.** |
| A07 head consistency | @dukesim (per-material μ); @abadi_2019_bones (5 discrete trabecular densities); @abadi_2023_emphysema (one density per region per phantom) | **Good physical motivation** for `label_to_table_density`. No empirical comparison found. |
| A08 U-Net vs conditional DDPM | @ho_2020, @palette_2022, @lyu_2022 (diffusion better); @moschetto_2025 (GAN better); @blau_2018 (distortion–perception tradeoff) | **Mixed evidence.** Expect U-Net to win on MAE. |
| A09 DDIM steps | @ddim_2021 | **Good.** |
| A10 first sample vs mean of 4 | @lyu_2022, @wolleb_2021 (averaging or ensembling improves accuracy); @blau_2018 (averaging trades texture for distortion) | **Good.** |
| A11 training-set size | Indirect only: @ron_mic_2015 ("very few images"); @valand_2026 (32 models) | **No learning-curve evidence for this task.** The listed @nnunet_2021 gives no such evidence. |
| A12 noise/blur stress test | @truect_challenge (50–150 mAs; reconstruction-dependent RMSE spread); @abadi_2023_emphysema (dose and kernel shift lung HU and MAE); @dukesim (noise model) | **Good** for choosing plausible magnitudes. |
| A13 residual / attention | @oktay_2018 | **Attention arm only.** The residual arm is unsupported by anything read; @nnunet_2021's residual-encoder variant results were not read. |
| A14 resolution | @truect_challenge (0.25 mm phantom vs ≈ 0.98 × 0.98 × 0.55 mm CT; scoring by linear upsampling); @nnunet_2021 (median-spacing resampling) | **Good.** |
| A15 volume-averaged vs point target | @truect_challenge (the challenge itself used linear interpolation onto the phantom grid); @abadi_2023_emphysema (edge-voxel errors); @abadi_2018_lung (sub-voxel vessels and airways) | **Good.** The listed @valand_2026 does not address it. |
| A16 reconstruction variant | @truect_challenge (5 algorithms gave widely different RMSE and SSIM); @abadi_2023_emphysema (kernel and algorithm effects); @valand_2026 (trained across 3 kernels) | **Good**, conditional on variants existing locally. |
| A17 noise/blur augmentation | @nnunet_2021 (Gaussian noise, blur and low-resolution augmentation are defaults); @abadi_2023_emphysema | **Partial.** @dukesim_copd_validation does not address augmentation. |
| A18 metadata conditioning | @truect_challenge (per-case mAs varies; DICOM-CT-PD carries tube current); @valand_2026 (multi-dose, multi-kernel training) | **Weak.** No paper read conditions on metadata. |
| A19 seed stability | @nnunet_2021 (5-fold ensembles as a variance reducer) | **Weak.** Methodological norm only. |

## 6. Where the literature questions the plan

1. *"XCAT-based voxel phantoms."* The emphysema models are new COPDGene-derived
   anatomies, built with XCAT-style lung and bone texture models. Only the
   liver-lesion models used the original XCAT library [@truect_challenge].
2. *Recon provenance.* The challenge distributed sinograms. The paper documents no
   standard "challenge-supplied reconstruction", no kernel and no quantitative HU
   calibration. The `recons/` folder must be characterised from its DICOM headers and
   from water and air ROIs, not assumed.
3. *Density varies per voxel* is unlikely. Density is per material label, with
   texture handled as discrete label bins (bones: 5 levels), plus one emphysema
   density per phantom [@abadi_2019_bones; @abadi_2023_emphysema]. A01, A05 and A07
   should be interpreted with this in mind, and E00 should confirm it.
4. The challenge ground truth is 64 keV mono-energetic HU, not density. A physically
   grounded intermediate target (μ at 64 keV from label + table) is available and was
   the challenge's own scoring target. The plan does not list it. It could serve as a
   sanity baseline at no cost.
5. Several plan reference attributions are not supported by the text read:
   @valand_2026 for A02, A05 and A15; @nnunet_2021 for A03 and A11;
   @dukesim_copd_validation for A17. See §5.

## 7. Seed-entry metadata check

All 12 seed DOIs and arXiv IDs resolve to the stated titles. Corrections and gaps:

- `dukesim`: issue year 2019 (vol. 38(6)), published online 2018-12-12. The plan's
  2019 is correct.
- `nnunet_2021`: online 2020-12-07, issue 2021 (vol. 18). OpenAlex lists 2020.
  Acceptable.
- `truect_challenge`: the plan omits authors. They are Abadi E, Segars WP, Felice N,
  … Samei E (13 authors), Medical Physics 2025.
- `dukesim_copd_validation`: the plan omits authors and DOI. They are Shankar SS,
  Jadick GL, Hoffman EA, Atha J, Sieren JC, Samei E, Abadi E. Proc. SPIE 12031,
  120313R (2022), doi:10.1117/12.2613212. Note that it validates against a
  **physical** phantom, not COPD patients.
- `cicek_2016`: the plan gives no DOI. The MICCAI DOI is
  10.1007/978-3-319-46723-8_49.
- `palette_2022`: published in SIGGRAPH 2022 (doi:10.1145/3528233.3530757); the
  arXiv version is 2021.
- `valand_2026`: correct (PMB 71(3) 035025, published 2026-02-13). **The PMC URL in
  the plan (PMC13173581) could not be loaded.** It redirected to a failing PDF, so the
  PMC ID is unconfirmed.
- `salinas_2025`: correct (BPEX 11(4) 045027).
